memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: But Balaam answered them, "Even if Balak gave me all the silver and gold in his palace, I could not do anything great or small to go beyond the command of the LORD my God. Now spend the night here so that I can find out what else the LORD will tell me." - Num 22:18-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Balaam's words sound wonderful. He declares that even a palace full of silver and gold could not make him go beyond the command of the Lord his God. It is the language of unwavering devotion, the kind of statement we might expect from a faithful prophet.

But then comes the telling next sentence. He asks the officials to stay another night so he can find out what else the Lord might say. Yet God had already spoken clearly. There was nothing else to discover. Balaam's request reveals a heart still hoping for a different answer.

This is a sobering picture. A person can say all the right things about obedience while quietly looking for a loophole. When God has spoken plainly, going back to ask again is not devotion; it is disguised disobedience. We too can pray for guidance we already have, hoping God will change His mind.

Genuine faith does not keep reopening settled questions in search of a more convenient answer. It rests in what God has said and obeys. In Christ we are called to a wholehearted trust that takes God at His word the first time. Beware the prayer that seeks not God's will but our own.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you ever keep asking God for guidance you have already received?
2. Where are you tempted to look for a loophole in God's clear command?
3. What would it mean to rest fully in what God has already said?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from reopening what You have settled, hoping for a different answer. Give me a heart that trusts Your word the first time and obeys wholeheartedly. Amen.
